rationale: Registered the successor execution for the vote-gate discriminator: the harness adds a vote_gate_after_restart case where one peer is demoted to a nonvoter while it keeps receiving entries, one voter follower is restarted alone, the leader is then stopped so the restarted instance knows no leader, and a real vote request carrying that nonvoter's own identity, address, term claim one above the responder's and its real last log entry is delivered over the real in-memory transport to the restarted instance. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the restarted instance held no configuration (responder_config_voters 0) and granted the vote (granted true), persisting the vote for the nonvoter at the claimed term; with the flag disabled the same request was refused (granted false, no vote persisted).

scope.description: Whether a restarted instance whose reconstruction is empty still enforces the committed configuration's voter gate when it decides whether to grant support. Thirteen in-process cases: the eleven previously exercised restart shapes plus a vote_gate_after_restart case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-peer cluster demotes one peer to a nonvoter while it keeps receiving entries, a voter follower is restarted alone, the leader is stopped so the restarted instance knows no leader, and the demoted peer's real transport delivers a real RequestVote to the restarted instance.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the restarted instance is reconnected to the two live peers in both directions.

The request represents the campaign of a peer whose own reconstruction still counts it as a voter, which is the mirror of the defect under audit: it carries that peer's real identity, address and last log entry, and claims a term one above the restarted instance's so that the request is not filtered by the duplicate-vote rule for a term in which the responder already voted during the cluster's initial election.

No responder state is fabricated: the request is delivered over the real transport to the real handler, and the responder's configuration, term and persisted vote are read back from its own memory and stable store.
Both peers hold the same last log entry, so the log up-to-dateness checks do not by themselves decide the request; the observation window after stopping the leader is 200 ms.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, pre-vote delivery, campaigns started by the target instance itself, and any claim about votes cast by peers other than the one delivering the request.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes one non-leader peer to a nonvoter, applies 20 entries so both peers hold the same log, reads the responder's own configuration entry, voter count and snapshot count, stops only the responder and emits a vote_inputs CA_EVENT, then rebuilds the responder over its own stores and reconnects it in both directions to the two live peers. It stops the leader, waits 200 ms, reads the responder's reconstructed configuration and term, and sends a RequestVoteRequest built from the demoted peer's own header, identity and last log entry with a term one above, through that peer's in-memory transport to the restarted instance. It then emits a vote_grant CA_EVENT with the responder's reconstructed voter count, its log's voter count, the granted flag, the response term, the responder's terms before and after, the candidate's membership and vote status in the committed configuration, and the vote term and candidate persisted in the responder's stable store before and after the request.
experiment.responsibility: requestVote owns the decision to grant support, and its membership and voter gates are the only checks that bind a node's vote to the committed configuration; the reconstructed configuration is what those gates read.

comparisons.description: Vote-path case with the flag enabled: a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in the responder's own log is not expected to receive the responder's vote.
Control: with the flag disabled the same request from the same peer is refused because that peer holds no vote in the responder's configuration.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the vote_gate_after_restart case with its flag-disabled control: a demoted nonvoter that holds the same log as the responder sends a real vote request over the real transport to a restarted instance that knows no leader, so the membership and voter gates of the vote path are exercised on the reconstructed configuration. Replaces the comparison set with the vote-path predicate and its control.
